html:
The Algerian Civil War was fought from 1992 to 2002 between the army-led government and armed Islamist groups. Algerians call it the black decade. Estimates of the dead run to about 150,000.

After riots in 1988, Algeria allowed many parties. The Islamic Salvation Front won the first round of elections in December 1991. In January 1992 the army cancelled the vote and banned the party, and Islamist guerrillas took up arms. The worst violence came in 1997 and 1998, when whole villages near Algiers were massacred.

The war wound down after President Abdelaziz Bouteflika offered amnesties from 1999. The memory of it kept many Algerians wary of upheaval for years, until the Hirak of 2019. See also Algeria and oil.
